$comment: Known, accepted npm audit advisories at high/critical severity.
Checked by scripts/audit-check.mjs, which FAILS CI on any high/critical
advisory NOT listed here — so new vulnerabilities break the build while
these known ones do not.
Every entry needs a reason and a reviewBy date. Entries that no longer
match anything are reported as stale so they get deleted rather than
silently widening the exception over time.
Phase 3B (Expo SDK 54 -> 57) cleared the four earlier entries (image-size x2,
postcss x2), which the gate then reported as stale and they were removed.
2026-10-12: the two entries below have NO patched release (latest braces 3.0.3
and node-forge 1.4.0 are the vulnerable versions) and are reached only through
build/dev tooling, never the deployed server or the apps. Re-check by reviewBy;
once a fixed version ships, `npm update braces node-forge` and delete the entry.
The same day, http-cache-semantics, shell-quote and source-map-js were fixed by
a lockfile-only update.
The 14 findings that remain are all MODERATE and therefore below this
gate's threshold. They sit in @expo/* build tooling and expo-router's
query-string/decode-uri-component chain at the latest published SDK, so
there is no version to upgrade to; npm's suggested 'fixes' for them are
downgrades to expo@46 / expo-router@5 and are not real.
2026-10-23: braces (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) is no longer reported and was removed
as stale. zod GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (fixed in 4.6.6): the zod 4 copy used by
eslint-plugin-react-hooks was updated to 4.6.7 (lockfile only); the zod 3 copy
inside @expo/cli has no patched 3.x release, so it is allowlisted below.
2026-10-29: decode-uri-component GHSA-qr28-fpjm-wq7f (high) appeared for the
expo-router -> query-string 7 -> decode-uri-component 0.2.2 chain above. The
fixed releases (0.5.1) are ESM-only: query-string 7 require()s the package and
calls it, which then throws 'is not a function' (checked), so an npm override
would break every route's params in both apps. npm's only real fix is
expo-router 58 (a new Expo SDK and new store builds). Allowlisted below until then.

allow.reason: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature forgery with low-exponent keys. No patched version exists (<=1.4.0 = latest). Reached only via @expo/cli and @expo/code-signing-certificates (Expo Updates code signing on a developer machine); we don't use Expo Updates code signing, and nothing at runtime loads node-forge.

Memory exhaustion when validating an oversized collection against a size-constrained schema. Fixed only in zod 4.6.6; the copy left is zod 3.25.76 (latest 3.x, no patched release) nested in expo/node_modules, used by @expo/cli's local dev server to validate dev-tools plugin settings from our own project config. It never sees user input and never runs in the deployed server (node dist/) or the apps. The zod 4 copy (eslint-plugin-react-hooks) is updated to 4.6.7.

Denial of service: decoding a long run of percent-encoded characters takes quadratic time. Reached only through expo-router -> query-string 7.1.3 -> decode-uri-component 0.2.2, in the rider and driver apps, where expo-router parses a URL's query string (our own navigation, and deep links). Not in the server, admin site or website. The worst case is a crafted campusride-rider:// or campusride-driver:// link that someone opens on their own phone, freezing that app until it is closed: no data exposed, nothing on the server. The fixed 0.5.1 is ESM-only and breaks query-string 7's require() (an override would break navigation); the real fix is expo-router 58, i.e. the next Expo SDK upgrade, which needs new store builds. Remove this entry then.
